why_this_run: Two advisories cannot support a claim of being better than the alternatives. This widens the comparison to cases nobody here chose, in classes this corpus does not obviously cover, and publishes whatever comes out.

case_selection.rule: the most recent reviewed advisories matching the filter, in API order, keeping those with a fix commit in the project's own repository
case_selection.note: The rule and its rejects were recorded on an earlier day, before any arm was run against them. What the rule cannot remove is that somebody typed the ecosystem and the severity, and that limitation travels with the cases.

targets.how_obtained: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<path>?ref=<parent-of-fix>, for every file the fix commit touched that existed before it
targets.files_the_fix_created: Two of new-api's five fix files did not exist before the fix (`common/request_body_limit.go`, `middleware/request_body_limit.go`). They are not in the target and cannot be: the vulnerable state of that advisory is the ABSENCE of a body limit, and what an auditor can see of it is the route table registering unauthenticated callbacks with no such middleware.

arms.treatment: the corpus as it ships: coverage.md routes, the packs it names, triage.md, the artifact contract
arms.control: the target, an output schema, and one instruction - senior application security engineer, own judgement, own method
arms.competitor: google/mantis at 5f76be0 (Apache-2.0), followed as written; nothing from it copied into this repository

scoring.file_level: deterministic, from the upstream fix commit
scoring.class_level: an independent context that sees only the advisory text and the finding text, and does not know which arm produced which finding
scoring.publication: every arm's result is published, including the ones where the corpus ties or loses

deviations_observed.$comment: Recorded as they happened, not assembled afterwards. Each one is noted because it cuts against a clean comparison, and two of the three favour an arm that is not ours.
deviations_observed.control_arm_ran_experiments: On `lima`, the no-corpus arm settled two triage questions by RUNNING shell constructs - whether an indirect expansion rescans for command substitution, and whether an unescaped value in an OpenRC conf file executes when sourced - and reported one of them as a finding on that basis. The instruction forbade executing the TARGET, and it did not execute the target; but it gave itself an experimental capability the corpus arm did not take, on the same files, in the same engagement. That is an advantage for the control arm and it is written here rather than left out.
deviations_observed.competitor_loses_a_stage: Reproduction and patching are stages of the competitor's own pipeline and this engagement forbids both, because the targets are file subsets with no build. Its rubric discounts findings that carry no reproduction evidence, so our constraint shows up inside its scores.
deviations_observed.new_api_evidence_is_an_absence: The defect there is the absence of a body limit. Two of the five fix files did not exist before the fix and cannot be in any target. Every arm is reading for something that is not there, which is the hardest shape to find and the easiest to argue about afterwards.

is_each_defect_visible_in_its_target.$comment: Checked by the run's author, not by any arm, and written before the blind judging ran. A case whose defect is not visible in the files given measures nothing about the arms, and saying so afterwards would be indistinguishable from an excuse.
is_each_defect_visible_in_its_target.vouch-proxy: Visible. The allocation the advisory names is in the one file given.
is_each_defect_visible_in_its_target.lima: Visible. The socket mode and the transport asymmetry the advisory turns on are in the files given.
is_each_defect_visible_in_its_target.new-api: Visible, and in the hardest shape there is. `constant/env.go` DECLARES `MaxRequestBodyMB`, `common/init.go` ASSIGNS it from `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_MB`, and nothing in the target consumes it - because the consumer is `common/request_body_limit.go` and `middleware/request_body_limit.go`, the two files the fix creates. So the vulnerable state, as seen from the three files given, is a configured limit with no enforcer, on a router that registers unauthenticated webhook POSTs. An arm can find it by asking who reads that constant.
